incident-bot: PagerDuty → page fired: HIGH - edge-tls-handshake-spike (pager duty incident 2445006789) :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Auto-escalation to oncall-sre triggered (rule: TLS-handshake-err > 5m)
samir (eng-sre): acked — looking now, oncall (anya) gets handoff in 2
anya (oncall): i'm on it. seeing lots of 525/526 from our edge load balancer, TLS handshake failures from multiple regions. dashboards show spike at 11:06 UTC.
ben (netops): confirmed — ALB target groups still healthy by HTTP, but TLS level shows many failed handshakes to edge cert chain. Might be cert chain mismatch after yesterday's rotation to new CA.
maria (support): customers reporting elevated 502/524 errors in EU lists, some timeouts. packet captures from a customer show `alert handshake failure` on ClientHello.
samir (eng-sre): grabbing curl + s_client from edge box to reproduce:
```
openssl s_client -connect edge01.redwood.example.com:443 -servername edge.redwood.example.com
```
openss output: `SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:no protocols available` and `certificate verify failed` depending on client cipher.
anya (oncall): quick check — Route53 weighted record update happened ~09:40 UTC. Could this be a partial rollout to a new edge fleet with different cert chain?
ben (netops): yes, the new fleet (edge-v2) was rolled and had certs from vendor B. Looks like some older clients don't like the new intermediate chain ordering.
kevin (infra lead): we need a mitigation path: either re-roll cert chain ordering on edge-v2 or shift traffic back to edge-v1. Which is faster?
samir (eng-sre): fastest is traffic shift. I can update weights to move 90% back to edge-v1 in Route53. Planning to do a staged rollback: 70% -> 90% -> 100%.
anya (oncall): start with 70% now. I'll watch error rates and customer impact. samir, ping me when each step completes. :thumbsup:
samir (eng-sre): doing Route53 CLI command now:
```
aws route53 change-weighted-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"edge.redwood.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"edge-v1","Weight":70,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.11.12.13"}]}}]}'
```
samir (eng-sre): weight -> 70% applied.
anya (oncall): metrics: TLS handshake error rate dropped ~60% within 60s. Latency still elevated for the minority of traffic stuck on edge-v2.
maria (support): sending customer note to impacted accounts: short blurb that we're mitigating, expected recovery in minutes.
ben (netops): to fix root cause we'll need to reorder the cert chain on edge-v2 or reissue with the old intermediate. I'm opening a ticket for cert ops.
kevin (infra lead): good. after 70 -> 90 -> 100, plan to keep edge-v2 out of rotation until certs validated. Also add a short-term healthcheck change to avoid marking targets degraded due to TLS negotiation quirks.
samir (eng-sre): applying next weight change to 90% now.
anya (oncall): 90% applied. Error rates down to baseline for most regions. Keeping observability alert active for another 15m.
pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded by samir (eng-sre). Auto-escalation suppressed.
maria (support): sent update to customers: "We've shifted traffic back to previous edge fleet; if you still see errors please DM us logs." Several replies said services recovered.
ben (netops): cert ops ticket: CERT-4123 created, assignee: taylor-certops. Plan: reissue intermediate chain matching old ordering, test in staging, then re-deploy to edge-v2.
kevin (infra lead): good. once CERT-4123 is resolved we'll schedule a controlled re-roll and add integration test for cert chain ordering.
anya (oncall): handoff note for night oncall: keep TLS handshake alert unmuted, do not perform cert rotations without staging verification. samir — can you post the short runbook snippet?
samir (eng-sre): runbook snippet (for handoff):
```
1) If TLS-handshake spikes: check Route53 weights -> reduce traffic to known-good fleet.
2) If handshake errors persist from a specific fleet: remove that fleet from LB rotation (set weight 0) and notify cert-ops.
3) Do not modify TTLs for >5m during mitigation.
4) After cert fix: test with openssl s_client and curl from two locations before reintroducing traffic.
```
anya (oncall): noted. handing off to night oncall (ben) in 20m. I'll close the PD incident once metrics stable for 15m.
samir (eng-sre): metrics stable for 12m, continuing to watch.
maria (support): last customer reply: "services normal now, thanks for quick response." :white_check_mark:
anya (oncall): closing loop — PD incident closed (manual) after 18m of stable metrics. filing post-incident notes and follow-ups: CERT-4123, ADD-238 (add chain-order test), and DOC-99 (runbook update).
kevin (infra lead): thanks team. good coordination. retrospective tomorrow. :coffee:
pagerduty: Incident 2445006789 closed by anya (oncall).
